title: Polymorphism and Dynamic Dispatch
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of polymorphism and dynamic dispatch using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates polymorphism and dynamic dispatch.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Polymorphism and Dynamic Dispatch** as part of **Inheritance, Interfaces, and Polymorphism**. Use interfaces and inheritance when they express substitutability, and prefer composition when an object should contain or coordinate collaborators. Use the subtopics—Subtyping and Substitutability, Runtime Method Dispatch, Polymorphic Collections—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Subtyping and Substitutability
items.text: Subtyping and Substitutability is one part of polymorphism and dynamic dispatch. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Runtime Method Dispatch
items.text: Runtime Method Dispatch means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Polymorphic Collections
items.text: Polymorphic Collections is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.
